# create-oikko-mongo
> Production-grade, modular MongoDB, Express, and TypeScript enterprise backend scaffolder by Oikko.

This file provides LLMs and AI Agents with complete context on `create-oikko-mongo`, including CLI execution syntax, non-interactive flags, architecture, and coding conventions.

## Quick Reference for AI Agents

When executing `create-oikko-mongo` from an AI Agent or automated script, ALWAYS use non-interactive flags to prevent TTY input blocking:

```bash
# Default setup (Recommended for AI agents):
npx create-oikko-mongo <project-name> --yes

# With custom parameters:
npx create-oikko-mongo <project-name> --roles "user,admin,seller" --port 8000 --pm npm --yes

# Fast scaffold without immediate npm install:
npx create-oikko-mongo <project-name> --yes --no-install
```

### CLI Command Options

- `[project-name]` (positional): Name of the target directory (default: `my-oikko-app`).
- `-y, --yes, --default`: Run in non-interactive mode using defaults.
- `-f, --force`: Overwrite target directory if it already exists.
- `--port <number>`: HTTP server port (default: `5000`).
- `--db <uri>`: MongoDB connection URI (default: `mongodb://localhost:27017/<project-name>`).
- `--roles <list>`: Comma-separated list of roles (e.g. `user, admin, seller`).
- `--pm <manager>`: Package manager (`npm` | `pnpm` | `yarn` | `bun`, default: `npm`).
- `--latest`: Forces latest npm versions for all dependencies.
- `--no-install`: Skips running `npm install`.
- `-h, --help`: Displays CLI help and exits.
- `-v, --version`: Displays package version and exits.

---

## Scaffolded Architecture & Project Layout

Each project bootstrapped by `create-oikko-mongo` strictly follows a modular enterprise architecture:

```
<project-name>/
├── src/
│   ├── app.ts                         # Express app configuration & middleware pipeline
│   ├── server.ts                      # Server bootstrap, DB & unhandled rejection handlers
│   └── app/
│       ├── config/                    # Config modules
│       │   ├── db.ts                  # Mongoose connection logic
│       │   ├── env.ts                 # Type-safe environment validation
│       │   ├── passport.ts            # Local & Google OAuth strategies
│       │   └── redis.config.ts        # Redis client & connection
│       ├── errorHelpers/              # Custom AppError class
│       │   └── appError.ts
│       ├── helpers/                   # Error parsers (Zod, Mongoose Cast, Duplicate Key)
│       ├── interfaces/                # Global type declaration merging
│       │   └── index.d.ts             # Express.Request user typing
│       ├── middlewares/
│       │   ├── checkAuth.ts           # JWT verification & RBAC authorization
│       │   ├── globalErrorHandler.ts  # Centralized HTTP error handler
│       │   ├── notFound.ts            # 404 Route handler
│       │   ├── requestLogger.ts       # Winston HTTP request logger
│       │   └── validateRequest.ts     # Zod request validation middleware
│       ├── modules/                   # Domain business modules
│       │   ├── auth/                  # Login, OAuth, tokens, password recovery
│       │   ├── otp/                   # OTP dispatch & verification
│       │   └── user/                  # User CRUD, profiles, roles
│       ├── routes/
│       │   └── index.ts               # Application router aggregation
│       └── utils/
│           ├── catchAsync.ts          # Async try-catch wrapper for controllers
│           ├── logger.ts              # Winston file & console logging
│           ├── sendEmail.ts           # Nodemailer / Resend email service
│           ├── sendResponse.ts        # Standardized API response utility
│           └── userTokens.ts          # JWT token signing & verification
├── .env                               # Auto-populated with cryptographically secure secrets
├── .env.example                       # Reference environment variables
├── .gitignore
├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json
```

---

## Coding Conventions for Generated Code

When an AI Agent writes code for an application created with `create-oikko-mongo`, adhere to these patterns:

### 1. Modular Directory Layout
Each feature lives in `src/app/modules/<featureName>/`:
- `<feature>.interface.ts`: TypeScript types and enums
- `<feature>.validation.ts`: Zod validation schemas
- `<feature>.model.ts`: Mongoose schema and model
- `<feature>.service.ts`: Business logic & database operations
- `<feature>.controller.ts`: HTTP request/response handlers wrapped in `catchAsync`
- `<feature>.route.ts`: Express routes with `validateRequest` and `checkAuth`

### 2. Controller Pattern
Always wrap controllers in `catchAsync` and respond using `sendResponse`:
```typescript
import { Request, Response } from "express";
import httpStatus from "http-status-codes";
import { catchAsync } from "../../utils/catchAsync";
import { sendResponse } from "../../utils/sendResponse";
import { ItemServices } from "./item.service";

const createItem = catchAsync(async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
    const result = await ItemServices.createItemService(req.body);
    sendResponse(res, {
        success: true,
        statusCode: httpStatus.CREATED,
        message: "Item created successfully",
        data: result,
    });
});
```

### 3. Error Handling
Never throw raw strings or generic errors. Throw `AppError`:
```typescript
import httpStatus from "http-status-codes";
import AppError from "../../errorHelpers/appError";

if (!item) {
    throw new AppError(httpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Item not found");
}
```

### 4. Role-Based Access Control
Enforce RBAC via `checkAuth`:
```typescript
import { Router } from "express";
import { checkAuth } from "../../middlewares/checkAuth";
import { Role } from "../user/user.interface";

router.post("/manage", checkAuth(Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPER_ADMIN), ItemController.manage);
```

### 5. Request Validation
Enforce payload validation using Zod:
```typescript
import { validateRequest } from "../../middlewares/validateRequest";
import { ItemValidation } from "./item.validation";

router.post("/", validateRequest(ItemValidation.createItemSchema), ItemController.createItem);
```
